مواضع ورود اللفظ ومشتقاته كلها، ثم الآيا: Every occurrence of the word and its derivatives, then verses that express the meaning without the word, with supporting exegesis, then the verses cited verbatim in hadith and scholarly statements.
أحكام الألباني وشعيب الأرنؤوط وأحمد شاكر: Gradings of al-Albani, Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut, Ahmad Shakir, Bashar Awwad Ma'ruf and others on the Sunan hadiths, as provided by the open Hadith API project, together with al-Tirmidhi's own verdict from the text of his Jami'.
The Lab writes nothing of its own and does not summarise. Everything in a paper is a text quoted from its source with its location, and the conclusion consists of figures computed from the texts. Weighing and deduction remain the researcher's work.
تُنقل من كل تفسير الجمل المتعلقة بالآية: From each tafsir, the sentences dealing with the verse and the topic are quoted verbatim, with chains of narration and poetic citations removed. If the topic is a phrase (such as "the Greatest Name of Allah"), it is searched for in the full texts of the tafsirs.
تطبيق مستقل لإعداد البحوث العلمية حول ال: A standalone app for preparing scholarly research on the Noble Quran, its words, attributes and questions, grounded in the Quran, the Sunnah and the approved books of tafsir. It works on phones and computers, and offline after the first visit.
يُحذف الإطار مثل «من الكتاب والسنة»، ويُ: Framing words such as "from the Quran and Sunnah" are removed, and each word is traced to its true root in the Mushaf. If a root has a wide range of meanings (such as the root s-m-w, which gives both "name" and "sky"), the search is limited to the form of the word itself.
يُبحث في متون الكتب الستة لا في أسانيدها: The search covers the texts (matn) of the Six Books, not their chains. The narrations of one hadith are gathered into a single entry with their numbers in each book; a hadith is identified by the same Companion narrator and close wording, and each narration's grading is given.
التفسير الميسر، وتفسير الجلالين، وتيسير: Al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, Tafsir al-Jalalayn, Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman by al-Sa'di, Ma'alim al-Tanzil by al-Baghawi, Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Jami' al-Bayan by al-Tabari, al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran by al-Qurtubi, and al-Muyassar fi Gharib al-Quran for word meanings.
صحيح البخاري (ترقيم فتح الباري)، وصحيح م: Sahih al-Bukhari (Fath al-Bari numbering), Sahih Muslim (Muhammad Fu'ad Abd al-Baqi numbering), Sunan Abi Dawud (Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid numbering), Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Ahmad Shakir numbering), Sunan al-Nasa'i (Abu Ghudda numbering) and Sunan Ibn Majah (Abd al-Baqi numbering).
لا يحوي المختبر بعدُ مسند أحمد ولا مستدر: The Lab does not yet include Musnad Ahmad, al-Hakim's Mustadrak, hadith commentaries (such as Fath al-Bari) or single-topic works (such as al-Suyuti's al-Durr al-Munazzam), so it neither cites nor quotes them. Where scholars in the included tafsirs refer to them, their words appear verbatim under "Statements of the scholars".

ورد الصباح والمساء من حصن المسلم بتخريجه: The morning and evening remembrances from Hisn al-Muslim with their sources, shown at the right time for your city.
أفضل وقتها الآن: من الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس: Its best time is now: from dawn until sunrise.
Its time is now; best is soon after dawn.
يمتد وقتها عند بعض العلماء إلى العصر، فإ: Some scholars extend its time until Asr; if you missed it, recite it now.
أفضل وقتها الآن: من العصر إلى غروب الشمس: Its best time is now: from Asr until sunset.
وقتها الآن، ويمتد عند كثير من العلماء إل: Its time is now; many scholars extend it into the early night.
يمتد وقتها عند كثير من العلماء في الليل،: Many scholars extend its time into the night; the morning remembrances begin at dawn.
قال الله تعالى: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِي: Allah says: “So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning” (al-Rum 30:17), and: “Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting” (Qaf 50:39).
تظهر أذكار الصباح من الفجر حتى العصر، وأ: Morning remembrances show from Fajr until Asr and evening remembrances from Asr until Fajr, calculated from your city's prayer times, and they work offline. The best morning time is between Fajr and sunrise and the best evening time between Asr and sunset, and you can open the other set at any time.
النصوص من كتاب «حصن المسلم من أذكار الكت: The texts are from Hisn al-Muslim by Dr Said ibn Ali ibn Wahf al-Qahtani, and the Quranic verses from the bundled Mushaf (Hafs). Each remembrance shows its source and grading faithfully; where hadith scholars differ on authenticity it is marked “Disputed grading”.
رفيقك اليومي: حفظ بخطة مراجعة، وأذكار ال: Your daily companion: memorisation with a review plan, morning and evening remembrances, and prayer times.
تظهر في وقتها حسب مدينتك، بنصوص حصن المس: Shown at the right time for your city, with the texts of Hisn al-Muslim and their sources, and a counter for each one.
§a.kursi.m: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast. Then Ayat al-Kursi (al-Baqarah 2:255).
§a.kursi.v: Whoever recites it in the morning is protected from the jinn until evening, and whoever recites it in the evening is protected from them until morning.
§a.kursi.s: Al-Hakim (1/562); graded authentic by al-Albani in Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/273)
§a.baqara.m: The last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah (2:285–286).
§a.baqara.v: Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.
§a.quls.m: Surat al-Ikhlas, Surat al-Falaq and Surat al-Nas, each beginning with the Basmala.
§a.quls.v: Whoever recites them three times in the morning and in the evening, they will suffice him against everything.
§a.quls.s: Abu Dawud (5082) and al-Tirmidhi (3575); see Sahih al-Tirmidhi (3/182)
§a.mulk.m: We have entered the morning, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah. Praise is to Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
§a.mulk.e: We have entered the evening, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah. Praise is to Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
§a.mulk.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it every morning and evening.
§a.bika.m: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
§a.bika.e: O Allah, by You we enter the evening and by You we enter the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return.
§a.bika.v: The Prophet ﷺ taught it to his Companions.
§a.bika.s: Al-Tirmidhi (3391) and Abu Dawud (5068); see Sahih al-Tirmidhi (3/142)
§a.sayyid.m: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
§a.sayyid.v: The master supplication for forgiveness: whoever says it with conviction in the evening and dies that night enters Paradise, and likewise in the morning.
§a.ushhid.m: O Allah, I have entered the morning calling You to witness, and calling the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all Your creation to witness, that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
§a.ushhid.e: O Allah, I have entered the evening calling You to witness, and calling the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all Your creation to witness, that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
§a.ushhid.v: Whoever says it four times, Allah frees him from the Fire.
§a.ushhid.s: Abu Dawud (5069); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.nima.m: O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation have this morning is from You alone, without partner. To You is the praise and to You is the thanks.
§a.nima.e: O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation have this evening is from You alone, without partner. To You is the praise and to You is the thanks.
§a.nima.v: Whoever says it in the morning has given thanks for his day, and whoever says it in the evening has given thanks for his night.
§a.nima.s: Abu Dawud (5073); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.afini.m: O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my body. O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my hearing. O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my sight. There is no god but You. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. There is no god but You.
§a.afini.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate with it three times every morning and evening.
§a.afini.s: Abu Dawud (5090) and Ahmad (5/42); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.hasbi.m: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
§a.hasbi.v: Whoever says it seven times in the morning and evening, Allah will suffice him in whatever concerns him of this world and the Hereafter.
§a.hasbi.s: Abu Dawud (5081) as a statement of Abu al-Darda; Shuayb and Abd al-Qadir al-Arnaut graded its chain authentic in their edition of Zad al-Maad (2/376)
§a.hasbi.n: It is authentically a Companion statement, and its words are in the Quran (al-Tawbah 9:129).
§a.afw.m: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from in front of me and behind me, from my right and my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being taken unawares from beneath me.
§a.afw.v: The Prophet ﷺ never left these supplications in the evening and the morning.
§a.afw.s: Abu Dawud (5074) and Ibn Majah (3871); graded authentic by al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah (2/332)
§a.alim.m: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of Satan and his call to associate partners with You, and from bringing evil upon myself or upon any Muslim.
§a.alim.v: The Prophet ﷺ taught it to Abu Bakr to say in the morning, in the evening and on going to bed.
§a.alim.s: Al-Tirmidhi (3392) and Abu Dawud (5067); see Sahih al-Tirmidhi (3/142)
§a.bismillah.m: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
§a.bismillah.v: Whoever says it three times in the morning and three times in the evening, nothing will harm him.
§a.bismillah.s: Abu Dawud (5088), al-Tirmidhi (3388) and Ibn Majah (3869); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.radit.m: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as my Prophet.
§a.radit.v: Whoever says it three times in the morning and evening, Allah has promised to please him on the Day of Resurrection.
§a.radit.s: Abu Dawud (5072), al-Tirmidhi (3389) and Ahmad (4/337); graded good by Ibn Baz in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.radit.n: The words themselves are authentic in Sahih Muslim (386), said on hearing the call to prayer.
§a.hayy.m: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, by Your mercy I seek help. Set right all my affairs, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
§a.hayy.v: The Prophet ﷺ advised Fatimah to say it every morning and evening.
§a.hayy.s: Al-Hakim (1/545), who graded it authentic with al-Dhahabi agreeing; graded good by al-Albani in Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/273)
§a.fath.m: We have entered the morning, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this day: its victory, its help, its light, its blessing and its guidance, and I seek refuge in You from the evil in it and the evil after it.
§a.fath.e: We have entered the evening, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this night: its victory, its help, its light, its blessing and its guidance, and I seek refuge in You from the evil in it and the evil after it.
§a.fath.s: Abu Dawud (5084); Shuayb and Abd al-Qadir al-Arnaut graded its chain good in their edition of Zad al-Maad (2/273)
§a.fitra.m: We have entered the morning upon the natural way of Islam, upon the word of sincere faith, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and submitting, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah.
§a.fitra.e: We have entered the evening upon the natural way of Islam, upon the word of sincere faith, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and submitting, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah.
§a.fitra.s: Ahmad (3/406–407) and Ibn al-Sunni in Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (34); see Sahih al-Jami (4/209)
§a.subhan.m: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him.
§a.subhan.v: Whoever says it a hundred times in the morning and evening, no one will bring anything better on the Day of Resurrection except one who said the same or more.
§a.tahlil10.m: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.
§a.tahlil10.v: Ten times, or once when tired; whoever says it ten times is like one who freed four souls from the descendants of Ismail.
§a.tahlil10.s: Sahih Muslim (2693); see Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/272)
§a.tahlil100.m: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.
§a.tahlil100.v: A hundred times in the morning: it equals freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds are written for him, a hundred sins are erased, and it protects him from Satan that day until evening.
§a.adad.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, as many times as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as heavy as His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words.
§a.adad.v: The Prophet ﷺ said them to Juwayriyah after the dawn prayer, and said that they would outweigh all she had said since morning.
§a.ilm.m: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and accepted deeds.
§a.ilm.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it after finishing the dawn prayer.
§a.ilm.s: Ibn Majah (925) and Ibn al-Sunni (54); graded authentic by al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah
§a.istighfar.m: I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.
§a.istighfar.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him a hundred times a day.
§a.kalimat.m: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
§a.kalimat.v: Whoever says it in the evening will not be harmed by any sting that night.
§a.kalimat.s: Sahih Muslim (2709), Ahmad (2/290) and al-Nasai in Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (590)
§a.salat.m: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.
§a.salat.v: Whoever sends blessings on me ten times in the morning and ten in the evening will receive my intercession on the Day of Resurrection.
§a.salat.s: Al-Tabarani; see Majma al-Zawaid (10/120) and Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/273)
§a.salat.n: Its chain is disputed; the virtue of sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ is authentic in Sahih Muslim (408).
دعا نوحٌ عليه السلام قومَه إلى عبادة الل: Noah (peace be upon him) called his people to worship Allah alone for a very long time: a thousand years less fifty. He was patient and never gave up.
أمره الله أن يصنع سفينة كبيرة، فكان قومه: Allah commanded him to build a large ship. His people passed by and mocked him, but he kept working with trust and certainty.
ولما جاء أمر الله، حمل في السفينة من كل: When Allah's command came, he carried in the ship a pair of every kind of animal, and the believers with him, and said: In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage.
جاء الطوفان، فجرت السفينة بمن فيها في مو: The flood came, and the ship sailed with everyone aboard through waves like mountains, and Allah kept them safe.
ثم أمر الله الأرض أن تبلع ماءها، والسماء: Then Allah commanded the earth to swallow its water and the sky to stop, and the ship came to rest safely on Mount Judi.
Being patient in doing good, however long it takes.
We obey Allah even if people make fun of us.
Safety comes with faith and good deeds.
كم سنة لبث نوح يدعو قومه؟: How many years did Noah call his people?
أين رست السفينة؟: Where did the ship come to rest?
ماذا حمل نوح في السفينة؟: What did Noah carry in the ship?
من كل زوجين اثنين والمؤمنين: A pair of every kind, and the believers
كان قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام يعبدون تماثي: Abraham's people (peace be upon him) worshipped statues they had made with their own hands. He asked them: What are these statues to which you are devoted?
فلما خرجوا، كسّر الأصنام كلها إلا كبيرها: When they went out, he broke all the idols except the biggest one, so that they would think and return to the truth.
سألوه: أأنت فعلت هذا؟ قال: بل فعله كبيره: They asked him: Did you do this? He said: Rather, this biggest one of them did it, so ask them, if they can speak. And they knew within themselves that idols cannot help and cannot speak.
غضبوا وألقوه في نار عظيمة، فقال الله: يا: They grew angry and threw him into a huge fire, and Allah said: O fire, be coolness and safety for Abraham. And he came out of it unharmed.
Only Allah deserves to be worshipped.
We use our minds, ask questions and think.
Whoever relies on Allah, Allah protects him.
ماذا قال الله للنار؟: What did Allah say to the fire?
لماذا كسر الأصنام؟: Why did he break the idols?
ليفكّر قومه أنها لا تنفع: So his people would think and see that they are useless
يونس عليه السلام رسول من الله. خرج من بل: Jonah (peace be upon him) was a messenger of Allah. He left his town angry with his people and boarded a ship full of people.
اضطربت السفينة، فاقترعوا فوقعت القرعة عل: The ship was in trouble, so they cast lots, and the lot fell on him. He was thrown into the sea, and a huge whale swallowed him.
في ظلمات الليل والبحر وبطن الحوت نادى: ل: In the darkness of the night, the sea and the whale, he called out: There is no god but You, glory be to You; I was indeed among the wrongdoers.
ولأنه كان من المسبّحين نجّاه الله، فألقا: Because he was one of those who glorified Allah, Allah saved him. The whale cast him onto the shore while he was ill, and Allah made a gourd plant grow over him.
ثم أرسله الله إلى قومه وهم مائة ألف أو ي: Then Allah sent him to his people, a hundred thousand or more. They all believed, and Allah let them enjoy life for a time.
ندعو الله في كل وقت، وهو يسمعنا حتى في ا: We call on Allah at every moment, and He hears us even in the dark.
We admit our mistakes and turn back to Allah.
Being patient and not getting angry.
ماذا قال يونس في بطن الحوت؟: What did Jonah say inside the whale?
لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمي: There is no god but You, glory be to You; I was indeed among the wrongdoers
ماذا أنبت الله عليه؟: What did Allah make grow over him?
خافت أم موسى على طفلها من فرعون، فألهمها: Moses' mother feared for her baby because of Pharaoh, so Allah inspired her: Nurse him, and when you fear for him, put him in the river, and do not fear or grieve; We will return him to you.
حمل الماءُ الصندوقَ فالتقطه آل فرعون، فق: The water carried the box, and Pharaoh's family picked it up. Pharaoh's wife said: A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us.
قالت أم موسى لأخته: تتبّعي أثره، فراقبته: Moses' mother said to his sister: Follow him. She watched him from afar, and the baby refused every nurse.
فدلّتهم أخته على أهل بيت يكفلونه، فردّه: His sister told them of a household that would care for him, so Allah returned him to his mother, that she might be content and not grieve, and know that Allah's promise is true.
Allah's promise is true and never fails.
Trusting Allah when we are afraid.
A clever sister helps her family.
أين وضعت أم موسى طفلها؟: Where did Moses' mother put her baby?
في صندوق في النهر: In a box on the river
قرة عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه: A comfort of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him
لماذا رُدّ موسى إلى أمه؟: Why was Moses returned to his mother?
كي تقرّ عينها ولا تحزن: So she would be content and not grieve
ورث سليمانُ أباه داود عليهما السلام، وعل: Solomon inherited from his father David (peace be upon them both). Allah taught him the language of birds and gave him of all things.
وجُمع لسليمان جنوده من الجن والإنس والطي: Solomon's soldiers of jinn, men and birds were gathered for him, and they marched in wonderful order.
فلما أتوا على وادي النمل قالت نملة: يا أ: When they came to the Valley of the Ants, an ant said: O ants, enter your homes so that Solomon and his soldiers do not crush you without noticing.
فتبسّم سليمان ضاحكاً من قولها، وشكر ربه:: Solomon smiled, amused at her words, and thanked his Lord: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me.
A leader protects those with them, as the ant did.
We thank Allah for His blessings.
الهدهد وملكة سبأ: The Hoopoe and the Queen of Sheba
تفقّد سليمانُ الطيرَ فلم يجد الهدهد، فقا: Solomon inspected the birds and did not find the hoopoe, so he said: Why do I not see the hoopoe?
جاء الهدهد وقال: جئتك من سبأ بنبأ يقين؛: The hoopoe came and said: I have come to you from Sheba with certain news. I found a woman ruling them, and she has a great throne.
ووجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله،: And I found her and her people bowing to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds seem good to them.
كتب سليمان كتاباً وأرسله مع الهدهد: إنه: Solomon wrote a letter and sent it with the hoopoe: It is from Solomon, and it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
وفي النهاية قالت الملكة: أسلمتُ مع سليما: In the end the queen said: I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
We check news before we pass it on.
We love what is good and invite to it with wisdom.
Obedience and reporting back (the hoopoe returned to tell).
من أين جاء الهدهد بالخبر؟: Where did the hoopoe bring the news from?
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
ماذا فعلت الملكة في النهاية؟: What did the queen do in the end?
أسلمت لله رب العالمين: She submitted to Allah, Lord of the worlds
فتية آمنوا بربهم، فزادهم الله هدى، وثبّت: Young men who believed in their Lord; Allah increased them in guidance and made their hearts firm upon the truth.
لجؤوا إلى الكهف ودعوا: ربنا آتنا من لدنك: They took refuge in the cave and prayed: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us right guidance in our affair.
ناموا في الكهف، والشمس تميل عنهم عند الش: They slept in the cave, the sun turning away from them at sunrise and sunset, and their dog stretching its forelegs at the entrance.
ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة سنين وازدادوا: They stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine, then Allah woke them.
أرسلوا أحدهم بنقودهم الفضية إلى المدينة: They sent one of them with their silver coins to the city to buy pure food, and told him to be gentle and careful.
Praying to Allah in hard times.
Good friends help us do good.
كم لبثوا في الكهف؟: How long did they stay in the cave?
ثلاثمائة سنين وازدادوا تسعاً: Three hundred years and nine more
من كان معهم عند باب الكهف؟: Who was with them at the cave entrance?
بماذا دعوا الله؟: What did they ask Allah for?
ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة: Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself
جاء جيش كبير معه فيل عظيم يريد هدم الكعب: A large army came with a mighty elephant, wanting to destroy the Kaaba, the House of Allah.
لكن الله أبطل مكرهم وجعل كيدهم في تضليل،: But Allah foiled their plan and made their scheme go astray, so they never reached what they wanted.
أرسل الله عليهم طيراً أبابيل، جماعات بعد: Allah sent against them birds in flocks, group after group, pelting them with stones of baked clay.
فصاروا كأوراق الزرع اليابسة التي أكلتها: They became like dry stalks eaten by cattle, and Allah protected His House.
Allah's power is greater than every power.
We never attack what is sacred to people.
ماذا أراد أصحاب الفيل؟: What did the People of the Elephant want?
ماذا أرسل الله عليهم؟: What did Allah send against them?
يوسف ورؤيا الكواكب: Joseph and the Dream of the Stars
رأى يوسف عليه السلام في منامه أحد عشر كو: Joseph (peace be upon him) saw in a dream eleven stars and the sun and the moon bowing to him, and his father told him: Do not tell your dream to your brothers.
حسده إخوته فألقوه في بئر عميقة، وأوحى ال: His brothers envied him and threw him into a deep well, and Allah inspired him that one day he would tell them what they had done.
مرّت قافلة فأرسلوا من يجلب الماء، فلما أ: A caravan passed by and sent someone to fetch water. When he let down his bucket he said: Good news! Here is a boy.
صبر يوسف حتى جعله الله أميناً على خزائن: Joseph was patient until Allah made him the trusted keeper of the storehouses of the land of Egypt, sharing out food fairly in the years of hardship.
جاءه إخوته فعفا عنهم وقال: لا تثريب عليك: His brothers came to him and he forgave them, saying: No blame upon you today; Allah will forgive you. And his dream came true.
Patience leads to a beautiful ending.
كم كوكباً رأى يوسف؟: How many stars did Joseph see?
أين ألقاه إخوته؟: Where did his brothers throw him?
ماذا قال لإخوته في النهاية؟: What did he say to his brothers in the end?
دعا صالحٌ عليه السلام قومَه ثمود: يا قوم: Salih (peace be upon him) called his people, Thamud: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.
جعل الله لهم ناقة آية، وقال صالح: ذروها: Allah gave them a she-camel as a sign, and Salih said: Let her eat on Allah's earth and do not touch her with harm.
لكنهم ظلموا فعقروا الناقة، فقال لهم: تمت: But they did wrong and killed the she-camel, so he told them: Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days.
نجّى الله صالحاً والمؤمنين معه برحمة منه: Allah saved Salih and the believers with him by His mercy, and seized the wrongdoers.
Keeping promises and not attacking others.
ما الآية التي أعطاها الله لثمود؟: What sign did Allah give to Thamud?
ماذا طلب صالح من قومه؟: What did Salih ask his people?
قال لقمان لابنه وهو يعظه: يا بني لا تشرك: Luqman said to his son, advising him: O my son, do not associate anything with Allah; associating others with Him is a great wrong.
ووصّى الله الإنسان بوالديه: حملته أمه وه: Allah has enjoined upon people care for their parents: his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness. Be grateful to Me and to your parents.
يا بني إنها إن تك مثقال حبة من خردل في ص: O my son, even if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed, inside a rock, or in the heavens or the earth, Allah will bring it forth.
يا بني أقم الصلاة، وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you.
ولا تصعّر خدّك للناس ولا تمش في الأرض مر: And do not turn your cheek away from people in pride, nor walk on the earth arrogantly; be moderate in your pace and lower your voice.
Kindness and gratitude to our parents.
Humility, a gentle voice and good manners.

نزل القرآن الكريم على النبي ﷺ من عند الل: The Noble Quran was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ from Allah through Gabriel (peace be upon him). The verses show that its revelation began in Ramadan, on the Night of Decree, and then it came down in parts, as events required, over about twenty-three years, so that Allah would strengthen the Prophet's heart and it would be recited to people at a measured pace.
ابتداء النزول في رمضان، في ليلة مباركة ه: Revelation began in Ramadan, on a blessed night: the Night of Decree.
نزل منجّماً (مفرّقاً) لا جملة واحدة، وذك: It came down in instalments, not all at once. Scholars mention among the wisdoms: strengthening the Prophet's heart ﷺ, easing memorisation and understanding, and the gradual giving of rulings.
الواسطة في النزول جبريل عليه السلام، الر: The bearer of revelation was Gabriel (peace be upon him), the Trustworthy Spirit.
اعتنى العلماء بمعرفة أول ما نزل من القرآ: Scholars took care to know the first and the last of the Quran to be revealed, since this shows the history and gradual order of the rulings and distinguishes the abrogating from the abrogated. The soundest view is that the opening of Surah Al-Alaq was revealed first, then the opening of Surah Al-Muddaththir after a pause in revelation. They differed over the last revealed, with several views, among them the verse "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah".
أول ما نزل على الإطلاق: «اقرأ باسم ربك ا: The very first revealed: "Read in the name of your Lord who created" up to "taught man what he did not know".
After the pause in revelation, the opening of Surah Al-Muddaththir came down.
في آخر ما نزل أقوال، ولا يُرفع منها قول: There are several views on the last revealed. None is explicitly attributed to the Prophet ﷺ; each reflects what a Companion knew.
المشهور عند العلماء أن المكي ما نزل قبل: The well-known view among scholars is that Makki is what was revealed before the Hijra and Madani what was revealed after it, even if in Makkah. This is known by transmission from the Companions and their Successors, not by reasoning alone. It helps in knowing abrogation, the history of the rulings, and the style of the call in each stage.
يغلب على المكي: الدعوة إلى التوحيد والبع: Makki passages mostly call to monotheism and the Resurrection, tell the stories of the prophets, have short verses, and address "O mankind".
يغلب على المدني: تفصيل الأحكام والحدود و: Madani passages mostly detail rulings, penalties and jihad, mention the People of the Book and the hypocrites, and address "O you who believe".
في عدد من السور خلاف بين العلماء في كونه: Scholars differ over whether some surahs are Makki or Madani, and some surahs contain excepted verses.
سبب النزول: ما نزلت الآية أو الآيات متحد: An occasion of revelation is an event or question that a verse or verses came down about, or whose ruling they explained, at the time it happened. It can only be known through sound reports from those who witnessed the revelation. Knowing it helps in understanding the verse and removing confusion, and according to most scholars the ruling follows the general wording, not the specific occasion.
لا يُعرف سبب النزول بالرأي، وإنما بالروا: Occasions of revelation are not known by opinion, only by sound reports from the Companions.
قد يتعدد السبب والنازل واحد، وقد تنزل آي: One passage may have several occasions, and several passages may share one occasion.
العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب، فيشمل: The ruling follows the general wording, not the specific occasion, so it covers everyone in the same situation.
جُمع القرآن ثلاث مرات: في عهد النبي ﷺ حف: The Quran was compiled three times: in the Prophet's time ﷺ, memorised in hearts and written on parchment, palm stalks and stone tablets; in the time of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, gathered into sheets after many reciters were martyred at al-Yamama; and in the time of Uthman ibn Affan, copied into mushafs in the dialect of Quraysh and sent to the major cities. Allah Himself has guaranteed its preservation.
الجمع الأول في عهد النبي ﷺ: حفظ في الصدو: First compilation, in the Prophet's time ﷺ: memorised in hearts and written separately in his presence.
الجمع الثاني في عهد أبي بكر: جمع ما كُتب: Second compilation, under Abu Bakr: what had been written was gathered into one set of sheets on Umar's advice, a task entrusted to Zayd ibn Thabit.
الجمع الثالث في عهد عثمان: نسخ المصاحف و: Third compilation, under Uthman: mushafs were copied and people united on them; from this comes the Uthmani script in which the Mushaf is written today.
الإتقان للسيوطي، النوع السادس عشر: في كي: Al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, type 16: how it was revealed; Manna al-Qattan, Mabahith fi Ulum al-Quran, section on revelation.
الإتقان للسيوطي، النوع السابع: معرفة أول: Al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, type 7: the first revealed, and type 8: the last revealed.
الإتقان للسيوطي، النوع الأول: معرفة المك: Al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, type 1: Makki and Madani; al-Zarkashi, al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Quran, type 9.
الإتقان للسيوطي، النوع التاسع: معرفة سبب: Al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, type 9: occasions of revelation; al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul; al-Suyuti, Lubab al-Nuqul.
الإتقان للسيوطي، النوع الثامن عشر: في جم: Al-Suyuti, al-Itqan, type 18: its compilation and order; Abu Shama, al-Murshid al-Wajiz.

قاله بعد أن سقى للمرأتين، وهو غريب جائع،: He said it after watering for the two women, a hungry stranger, and Allah opened the way for him.

Seeking refuge from the whisperings of the devils and their presence.

تواضع وحلم وقيام بالليل واعتدال في الإنف: Humility, forbearance, night prayer and moderation in spending.

أباح الله التعدد إلى أربع بشرط العدل، فإ: Allah permitted marrying up to four on condition of justice; if injustice is feared, then only one.

Why was man created, and what is his function on earth? The answer from the Holy Quran with its verses and their exegesis from the major tafsir works, and from the authentic Sunnah with references, in nine chapters ending with "If only I had sent ahead for my life".

أدوات بيانية درسها علماء البلاغة في القر: Rhetorical devices studied by scholars of balagha in the Quran, often gathered in a single verse. Their shared purpose is that meaning be seen and felt, not merely known.
نصوص الآيات بلفظ مصحف المدينة النبوية (م: Verse texts follow the Madinah Mushaf (King Fahd Complex, version #) in its script; hadith texts come from the bundled two Sahihs with their numbering; exegetes are quoted verbatim from their works bundled in Mishkat (al-Sa'di, al-Qurtubi, Ibn Kathir, al-Baghawi); introductions and image notes are concise summaries. The tafsirs of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) and Ibn 'Ashur (al-Tahrir wa al-Tanwir) are not bundled in Mishkat, so nothing is quoted from them.
التصوير في القرآن: المعنى صورةً حية: Imagery in the Quran: meaning as a living picture
من أبرز خصائص البيان القرآني أنه يعرض ال: One of the most striking features of Quranic expression is that it presents abstract meanings, inner states and unseen events in tangible, moving images, so the reader sees them with the imagination and feels them in the heart. For this Allah has varied every kind of parable in the Quran and made parables a path to remembrance and understanding.
وصف القرآن بأنه أحسن الحديث، متشابه في ح: The Quran is described as the best of speech, consistent in its beauty; skins shiver from it, then soften. Its beauty leaves a visible mark on bodies and hearts.
تصريف الأمثال وتنويعها مقصد من مقاصد الق: Varying and diversifying parables is one of the aims of the Quran, to bring meaning close to every soul.
وما يعقلها إلا العالمون: Only those of knowledge understand them
الأمثال ظاهرها قريب، وفقهها لأهل العلم؛: Parables are near in their surface and deep in their understanding, joining the pleasure of the image to the depth of meaning.
لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل: Had We sent down this Quran upon a mountain
صورة مفترضة تهزّ القلب: الجبل الأصم يخشع: A supposed image that shakes the heart: the solid mountain would humble itself and split apart, so what of a living heart?
يضرب القرآن الأمثال من مشاهد يعرفها النا: The Quran draws its parables from scenes people know: the lamp, the tree, the ear of grain, the mirage, the sea, the spider and the rain. It links the unseen meaning to a present image and weighs truth against falsehood before the eye, then before the mind.
مثل نوره كمشكاة: The parable of His light is like a niche
تمثيل مركّب: مشكاة فيها مصباح، في زجاجة: A compound parable: a niche with a lamp, in a glass like a brilliant star, lit from the oil of a blessed tree; light upon light.
الكلمة الطيبة والكلمة الخبيثة: The good word and the evil word
شجرة أصلها ثابت وفرعها في السماء، تقابله: A tree firmly rooted with its branches in the sky, set against a tree uprooted from the earth: two opposing images of faith and disbelief.
حبة أنبتت سبع سنابل: A grain that grows seven ears
صورة النماء: حبة واحدة تصير سبعمائة، فير: An image of growth: a single grain becomes seven hundred, so the one who spends sees the multiplied reward with his own eyes.
مثلان لأعمال الكفار: سراب يحسبه الظمآن م: Two parables of the deeds of disbelievers: a mirage the thirsty takes for water, and layers of darkness in a deep sea.
من اتخذ من دون الله أولياء كمن احتمى ببي: Whoever takes protectors besides Allah is like one sheltering in a spider's house, the frailest of houses.
دورة كاملة في آية: ماء، ثم نبات مختلط نا: A whole cycle in one verse: water, then lush mingled plants, then dry stalks scattered by the winds.
مثل المنافق: نار أضاءت ما حوله ثم ذهب ال: The parable of the hypocrite: a fire that lit what was around him, then Allah took away its light and left him in darkness, unable to see.
رماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف؛ صورة لأ: Ashes blown by a strong wind on a stormy day: an image of deeds that vanish and leave nothing behind.
تختصر الاستعارة الصورة في كلمة، وتلمّح ا: Metaphor condenses an image into one word, metonymy hints at a meaning through what accompanies it with refinement and discretion, and personification breathes life into the inanimate and into time: the day is "stripped" from the night, the dawn "breathes", and humility becomes a "wing" that is lowered.
واشتعل الرأس شيباً: My head has blazed with grey
شبّه انتشار الشيب في الرأس باشتعال النار: The spread of grey hair is likened to the blaze of fire, condensing all of old age into three words.
جناح الذل من الرحمة: The wing of humility out of mercy
صورة الطائر يخفض جناحه لفراخه رحمة وحنوا: The image of a bird lowering its wing over its young in tenderness clothes kindness to parents in mercy.
والصبح إذا تنفس: And the dawn when it breathes
الليل يعسعس مقبلاً ومدبراً، والصبح يتنفس: The night approaches and departs, and the dawn breathes as a living being breathes after constriction: personification that turns time into a living creature.
نسلخ منه النهار: We strip the day from it
جُعل ذهاب الضوء كسلخ الجلد عن الذبيحة، ف: The departure of light is made like stripping a hide, so the night appears as the original and the day as a covering over it.
أُسندت الإرادة إلى الجدار لميله وإشرافه: "Wanting" is ascribed to the wall because it leaned on the verge of falling, so the scene itself speaks of danger.
يد مغلولة وبسط كل البسط: A chained hand and a hand fully open
كناية عن البخل بالغلّ، وعن الإسراف بالبس: Miserliness pictured as a chained hand and extravagance as a hand fully open, then the image of sitting blamed and destitute.
هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن: They are a garment for you and you for them
اللباس ستر ودفء وقرب وزينة؛ صورة واحدة ت: A garment covers, warms, stays close and adorns: one image gathering the meanings of affection between spouses, together with a refined allusion to intimacy.
أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتاً: Would one of you like to eat his dead brother's flesh?
صُورت الغيبة بأبشع صورة تنفر منها الطباع: Backbiting is pictured in the most repulsive image nature recoils from, so the listener hates it by law as he hates that by instinct.
المشاهد الكونية: جمال الخلق المنظور: Cosmic scenes: the visible beauty of creation
يدعو القرآن إلى النظر في الكون نظرة تأمل: The Quran invites us to look at the universe with reflection and wonder: the built and adorned sky, the raised mountains, the outspread earth, the driven clouds, the plants that stir and swell. In a single verse it joins the proof of power to the delight of beauty.
أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت: Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?
أربع لوحات في مشهد البادية: الإبل، والسم: Four panels of the desert scene: camels, sky, mountains and earth. The Arab saw them every day, and the Quran invites him to see them anew.
السماء بنيناها وزيناها: We built the sky and adorned it
سماء بلا فروج، وأرض ممدودة، وزوج بهيج، و: A sky without rifts, an outspread earth, every delightful kind, and tall palms with clustered spathes: words that carry beauty as they carry proof.
انظروا إلى ثمره إذا أثمر وينعه: Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and ripens
أمر صريح بالنظر إلى الثمر في أطواره حتى: An explicit command to look at fruit through its stages until it ripens: contemplating beauty is worship the Quran calls to.
يزجي سحاباً ثم يجعله ركاماً: He drives the clouds, then piles them up
مشهد متتابع الحركة: سوق السحاب، ثم تأليف: A scene of successive movement: driving the clouds, joining them, piling them up, rain pouring from within, and lightning that almost takes away sight.
يرسل الرياح فتثير سحاباً: He sends the winds and they stir up clouds
الرياح تثير، والسحاب يُبسط ويُجعل كسفاً،: The winds stir, the clouds spread and break into fragments, rain falls from within, then the joy of those who receive it.
الأرض الهامدة تهتز وتربو إذا نزل الماء،: The lifeless earth stirs and swells when water falls on it, and grows every delightful kind: an image of life after death.
حتى عاد كالعرجون القديم: Until it returns like an old date stalk
الشمس تجري لمستقر لها، والقمر يتنقل في م: The sun runs to its resting place, and the moon moves through its phases until it returns like a dry, curved date stalk; each swims in an orbit.
مشاهد القيامة: Scenes of the Day of Resurrection
يرسم القرآن يوم القيامة مشاهد حاضرة كأنه: The Quran paints the Day of Resurrection in scenes present as if happening before the eyes: the sun is wrapped up, mountains pass like clouds and become like fluffed wool, people are like scattered moths, and the nursing mother forgets her infant, so the reader lives the terror before it comes and prepares for it.
إذا الشمس كورت: When the sun is wrapped up
اثنا عشر مشهداً متتابعاً بأداة واحدة «إذ: Twelve successive scenes introduced by the same word "when", then the answer: "a soul will know what it has brought"; a rhythm that takes the breath away.
الناس كالفراش المبثوث في حيرته وتهافته،: People like scattered moths in their confusion and rushing, mountains like fluffed wool in their lightness: two similes that turn the image of strength into weakness.
تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت: Every nursing mother will forget her infant
أقوى العواطف وأرسخها تنقطع من الهول، وتر: The strongest and firmest of emotions is cut off by terror, and you see people as if drunk while they are not drunk.
يوم يفر المرء من أخيه: The Day a man will flee from his brother
الصاخة تصك الآذان، ثم مشهد الفرار بترتيب: The Deafening Blast strikes the ears, then the scene of flight, ascending from brother to mother and father, then wife and children.
كأنهم جراد منتشر: As if they were scattered locusts
خروج الناس من القبور في كثرتهم واضطرابهم: People coming out of their graves in their multitude, agitation and spread like locusts, with their eyes humbled.
الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمضي مضي السحاب،: You think the mountains are still while they pass as clouds pass: the scene joins apparent stillness to hidden motion.
فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة: When the Horn is blown with a single blast
نفخة واحدة تُحمل بها الأرض والجبال فتدكا: One blast, and the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing, and the sky splits, frail on that Day.
يصور القرآن خلجات النفس كما يصور مشاهد ا: The Quran portrays the stirrings of the soul as it portrays the scenes of the universe: a chest so constricted it is as if climbing into the sky, the wide earth narrowing for the distressed, hearts reaching the throats in fear, a mother's heart becoming empty, and the wrongdoer biting his hands in regret.
كأنما يصعد في السماء: As though climbing into the sky
انشراح الصدر للهدى يقابله صدر ضيق حرج، ك: A chest opened to guidance is set against a chest tight and constricted, like one straining to climb into the sky with his breath growing short.
ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت: The earth closed in on them despite its vastness
حال الثلاثة الذين خُلّفوا: الأرض على سعت: The state of the three who were left behind: the earth, vast as it is, closed in, and their own souls closed in, until they were certain there was no refuge except in Allah.
تصوير لشدة الخوف يوم الأحزاب: زاغت الأبص: A portrayal of extreme fear on the day of the Confederates: eyes shifted and hearts almost left their places.
وأصبح فؤاد أم موسى فارغاً: The heart of Moses' mother became empty
قلب خلا من كل شيء إلا من ذكر ولدها، حتى: A heart emptied of everything except thought of her child, so that she nearly revealed him, had Allah not strengthened her heart.
حزن يعقوب عليه السلام صُور أثراً في العي: Jacob's grief is pictured as a mark on the eye and as suppressed sorrow in the heart that complains to none but Allah.
ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه: The Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands
حركة جسدية تختصر الندم كله: يعض على يديه: A bodily gesture that sums up all regret: he bites his hands and wishes he had taken a path with the Messenger.
صورة النفس بين الجزع عند الشر والمنع عند: A portrait of the soul between panic in hardship and withholding in ease, after which the Quran makes an exception of those who pray.
دعانا لجنبه أو قاعداً أو قائماً: He calls on Us lying, sitting or standing
الإنسان في الضر يدعو على كل أحواله، فإذا: In hardship man calls on Allah in every posture; once relieved, he passes on as if he had never called: a true picture of the soul's fickleness.
الجمال والزينة في القرآن: Beauty and adornment in the Quran
ذكر القرآن الجمال والزينة في الخلق والنع: The Quran mentions beauty and adornment in creation and its blessings: the beauty of livestock when they return in the evening and go out in the morning, the adornment of stars in the sky, gardens full of delight, and Allah perfecting the form of man. It permits adornment to His servants and makes the adornment of the earth a test, not an end.
ولكم فيها جمال: And for you in them is beauty
ذكر الجمال بلفظه بعد المنافع، فالنعمة في: Beauty is named explicitly after benefits: the blessing of livestock is both usefulness and a sight to behold.
الخيل والبغال والحمير للركوب والزينة، وا: Horses, mules and donkeys are for riding and for adornment; adornment is a recognised purpose in creation.
خذوا زينتكم عند كل مسجد: Take your adornment at every place of prayer
أمر بالتزين للصلاة، وإنكار على من حرّم ز: A command to adorn oneself for prayer, and a rebuke to anyone who forbids the adornment Allah brought forth for His servants and the good things of provision.
زينة لها لنبلوهم: An adornment for it, to test them
زينة الأرض ميدان ابتلاء: أيهم أحسن عملاً: The adornment of the earth is a field of testing: which of them is best in deed. Beauty is a means, not an end.
بزينة الكواكب: With the adornment of the stars
السماء الدنيا مزينة بالكواكب، فالنظر إلي: The nearest heaven is adorned with stars; looking at it is both delight and lesson.
البهجة: الحسن الذي يبهج الناظر، وقد نفى: Delight is the beauty that gladdens the onlooker, and it is denied that they could ever make its trees grow.
الإحسان في الخلق عام لكل شيء، فكل مخلوق: Excellence in creation covers everything: every creature is in the best form befitting it.
وصوركم فأحسن صوركم: He formed you and perfected your forms
المصور سبحانه أحسن صورة الإنسان، فالشكر: The Fashioner perfected the form of man, so gratitude for beauty of form is like gratitude for every other blessing.
جواب القسم بالتين والزيتون وطور سينين وا: The answer to the oath by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and the secure city: man was created in the most balanced form and shape.
الجميل في الأخلاق: الصبر الجميل والصفح ا: Beauty in character: beautiful patience and beautiful pardon
لم يقصر القرآن الجمال على الصور، بل وصف: The Quran does not limit beauty to forms; it describes the acts of the soul with it: beautiful patience with no complaint except to Allah, beautiful pardon with no reproach, beautiful distancing with no harm, and a beautiful release that preserves dignity at parting. It calls to repel evil with what is better.
قالها يعقوب عليه السلام حين جاؤوا على قم: Jacob said it when they brought Joseph's shirt with false blood, then sought Allah's help.
فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعاً: Beautiful patience; perhaps Allah will bring them all to me
تكررت الكلمة في المصيبة الثانية، ومعها ا: The phrase is repeated at the second calamity, now with hope: beautiful patience is inseparable from thinking well of Allah.
فاصبر صبراً جميلاً: So be patient with a beautiful patience
أمر للنبي ﷺ بالصبر على أذى قومه صبراً لا: A command to the Prophet ﷺ to bear his people's harm with patience free of panic and weariness.
فاصفح الصفح الجميل: So pardon with a beautiful pardon
الصفح الجميل: عفو بلا أذى، يقابل الإساءة: Beautiful pardon: forgiving without harm, meeting wrong with kindness.
واهجرهم هجراً جميلاً: And leave them with a beautiful leaving
حتى الهجر له جمال: إعراض بلا عتاب ولا أذ: Even distancing has its beauty: turning away without reproach or harm.
وسرحوهن سراحاً جميلاً: And release them with a beautiful release
الفراق نفسه يُطلب فيه الجمال: متعة وإحسا: Beauty is required even in parting: a gift, kindness and preserved dignity.
صورة العدو يتحول ولياً حميماً بالإحسان،: The image of an enemy becoming a devoted friend through kindness; none attains it but one of great fortune.
وقولوا للناس حسناً: And speak to people good words
جمال القول من جملة الميثاق المأخوذ على ب: Beautiful speech is part of the covenant taken from the Children of Israel, alongside tawhid and kindness to parents.
إلحاق أمر بأمر في صفة جامعة بينهما، فيُر: Joining one thing to another through a shared quality, so an abstract meaning is seen in a tangible form: the light of faith is a lamp in a niche, the good word is a good tree.
Example: "The parable of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp."
تشبيه طُوي أحد طرفيه، فتُنقل الكلمة إلى: A simile with one side folded away, so a word carries a new meaning and the whole image is condensed into one expression: the head "blazes" with grey hair as fire blazes.
Example: "And my head has filled (blazed) with white."
التعبير عن المعنى بلازمه، فيُفهم المقصود: Expressing a meaning through what accompanies it, so the intent is grasped from its image without being stated: a hand chained to the neck pictures extreme miserliness.
Example: "And do not make your hand chained to your neck."
إلباس الجماد والمعاني صفات الأحياء، فيتح: Clothing inanimate things and ideas with the traits of living beings, so the scene moves and breathes: the dawn breathes, the wall "wants" to collapse.
Example: "And by the dawn when it breathes."
مثل المؤمن الذي يقرأ القرآن كالأترجة: The believer who recites the Quran is like a citron
تمثيل نبوي بالحواس: الريح للظاهر والطعم: A prophetic parable through the senses: scent for the outward and taste for the inward. The Quran perfumes its reciter outwardly, and faith sweetens him inwardly.
مثلي ومثل الأنبياء كرجل بنى بيتاً فأحسنه: My example and that of the prophets: a man who built a beautiful house
صورة بناء جميل كامل إلا لبنة، فكانت الرس: The image of a beautiful, complete building missing one brick: the final message completed its beauty.
مثل المؤمنين في توادهم كمثل الجسد: The believers in their mutual love are like one body
تشبيه الجماعة بالجسد الواحد يصور التراحم: Likening the community to one body makes compassion tangible: when one limb aches, the whole body stays awake for it.
إن الله جميل يحب الجمال: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
حب الجمال في الثوب والنعل ليس كبراً؛ فال: Loving beauty in clothing and footwear is not arrogance: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, while arrogance is rejecting the truth and despising people.
إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم: Allah does not look at your forms
الجمال الذي يُوزن عند الله جمال القلب وا: The beauty weighed by Allah is the beauty of the heart and of deeds; forms and wealth are not what reward depends on.
إن الله كتب الإحسان على كل شيء: Allah has prescribed excellence in everything
الإحسان جمال الفعل في كل شيء، حتى في الذ: Excellence is the beauty of action in everything, even in slaughter, so how much more in dealing with people?
The beauty of the Quran lies in its wording and its meaning together.

القسم بالتين والزيتون: The oath by the fig and the olive
أقسم الله بشجرتين مباركتين وبمواطن الرسا: Allah swears by two blessed trees and by the lands of revelation, an oath that honours what is sworn by.
النخل والأعناب والزيتون والرمان من ماء و: Palms, vines, olives and pomegranates from a single water, then the command to look at the fruit as it forms and ripens: an invitation to reflect on food before eating it.
كلوا من ثمره وآتوا حقه: Eat of its fruit and give its due
جمعت الإباحة والشكر والنهي عن الإسراف في: Permission, gratitude and the prohibition of extravagance gathered in a single verse.
يُسقى بماء واحد ويُفضَّل بعضها على بعض ف: Watered with one water, yet some excel others in taste

O Allah, we ask You for al-Firdaws al-A'la, the highest part of Paradise.

The descriptions of Paradise are true in their reality, and their full nature is known only to Allah.

The descriptions in the Quran use familiar names to bring the meaning near, while their true reality is known only to Allah.

منازل عالية مبنية بعضها فوق بعض، تجري من: Lofty dwellings built one above another, with rivers flowing beneath them.

تجري الأنهار من تحت قصور الجنة وأشجارها:: Rivers flow beneath the palaces and trees of Paradise: rivers of water, milk, wine and honey that never spoil, springs whose drink is mixed with camphor, ginger and Tasnim, and al-Kawthar, a river given to the Prophet ﷺ.
ماء غير آسن، ولبن لم يتغير طعمه، وخمر لذ: Water that never stagnates, milk whose taste never changes, wine delicious to those who drink, and purified honey; and with all this, forgiveness from their Lord.
أكثر صفات الجنة ذكراً في القرآن جريان ال: The most frequently mentioned feature of Paradise in the Quran is rivers flowing beneath it; its fruits look alike but differ in taste.

في الجنة مساكن طيبة وغرف عالية وخيام من: Paradise has pleasant dwellings, lofty chambers and tents of hollow pearl, trees whose extended shade no sun breaks, raised couches and furnishings lined with brocade, with neither heat nor cold.

مساكن طاب منظرها ومقامها، في جنات إقامة: Dwellings pleasing to see and to live in, in gardens of lasting residence.
يُجزون الغرفة بما صبروا: They will be rewarded with the high chamber for their patience
الغرفة: المنزل العالي في الجنة، جزاء الص: The chamber is the lofty dwelling of Paradise, the reward of patience, where they are met with greetings and peace.

شجر بلا شوك، وثمر منضود، وظل لا ينقطع، و: Trees without thorns, fruit layered in rows, unending shade, flowing water, and fruit neither cut off nor forbidden.
جوّها معتدل لا حرّ فيه ولا برد، وظلالها: Its climate is temperate, with no heat and no cold; its shade is near and its fruit hangs low.
سرر مرفوعة ونمارق مصفوفة: Raised couches and cushions in rows
جنة عالية، لا لغو فيها، وعين جارية، وسرر: A lofty garden with no idle talk, a flowing spring, couches, cups, cushions and spread carpets.
طعامهم وشرابهم ولباسهم وحليهم: Their food, drink, clothing and adornment
يأكل أهل الجنة ويشربون تلذذاً لا عن جوع: The people of Paradise eat and drink for delight, not from hunger or thirst, from vessels of gold and silver; they wear silk, fine silk and brocade, and are adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls.
أساور من ذهب وثياب خضر: Bracelets of gold and green garments
حلية من ذهب، وثياب خضر من رقيق الحرير وغ: Adornment of gold and green garments of fine and heavy silk, reclining on adorned couches.
ولباسهم فيها حرير: Their garments there will be silk
Adornment of gold and pearls, and garments of silk.

آنية من فضة في صفاء الزجاج، قُدّرت على ق: Vessels of silver as clear as glass, measured exactly to their need.
يختارون من الفاكهة ما شاؤوا، ومن لحم الط: They choose whatever fruit they like, and whatever bird meat they desire.
عيشة راضية، وقطوف دانية، وطعام هنيء جزاء: A pleasing life, fruit hanging near, and wholesome food as reward for the deeds they sent ahead.

خمر الجنة بيضاء لذيذة، لا تذهب العقل ولا: The wine of Paradise is white and delicious; it neither takes away the mind nor brings headache.
أهل الجنة إخوان على سرر متقابلين، نُزع م: The people of Paradise are brothers on couches facing one another, with all rancour removed from their hearts; no toil, grief or death touches them, Allah joins their offspring to them, and their speech is glorification and peace.
ونزعنا ما في صدورهم من غل: We will remove whatever rancour is in their hearts
سلامة القلوب من الحسد والضغينة، وأمن من: Hearts free of envy and resentment, and security from toil and from ever being expelled.
الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن: Praise be to Allah, who has removed all grief from us

مقام أمين، وجنات وعيون، وأزواج من الحور: A secure station, gardens and springs, spouses of the hur al-'in, and no death after the first death.

أعلى نعيم أهل الجنة النظر إلى وجه الله ا: The highest bliss of the people of Paradise is looking upon the Noble Face of Allah, and His good pleasure upon them, after which He will never be displeased with them. This is the "increase" the Prophet ﷺ explained with his words "then He removes the veil".
Radiant, beautiful faces, looking at their Lord with their own eyes.
الحسنى: الجنة، والزيادة: النظر إلى وجه ا: The best reward is Paradise, and the "more" is looking upon the Face of Allah, as the Prophet ﷺ explained in the hadith of Suhayb.

The good pleasure of Allah is greater than all the delights of the gardens.
The radiance of bliss is recognised on their faces.

It is surrounded by hardships.
الإنفاق في السراء والضراء، وكظم الغيظ، و: Spending in ease and hardship, restraining anger, pardoning people, seeking forgiveness and not persisting in sin.

الاستقامة على التوحيد والطاعة، تبشّرهم ب: Steadfastness on tawhid and obedience; the angels give them glad tidings of it: a welcome from One Forgiving, Merciful.

Piety is the all-embracing quality of those who inherit Paradise.
الاسم العام لدار الثواب، وأصلها البستان: The general name of the abode of reward; the word originally means a garden so dense with trees that its shade covers what lies beneath.
أعلى الجنة وأوسطها، فوقه عرش الرحمن ومنه: The highest and central part of Paradise; above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, as in the hadith of al-Bukhari.
من «عَدَن بالمكان» إذا أقام به: جنات إقا: From "'adana", to reside permanently: gardens of everlasting residence that their people never leave.

المقام الذي أمن أهله فيه من كل خوف وحزن: The station where its people are safe from all fear, grief and loss.
مجلس حق لا لغو فيه ولا تأثيم، عند مليك م: A seat of truth, free of idle talk and sin, in the presence of a Sovereign, Perfect in Power.

«ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان» آنيتهما وما في: "For whoever fears standing before his Lord are two gardens", their vessels and all within them of gold.

هذه أسماء لدار واحدة باعتبار صفاتها، فكل: These are names of one abode, each pointing to an aspect of its bliss; some of them also name particular ranks within it, such as Firdaws. أصغر موضع في الجنة خير من الدنيا كلها، ف: The smallest space in Paradise is better than the whole world; then what of its dwellings?

الجنة درجات بعضها فوق بعض، والفردوس أوسط: Paradise has levels one above another, and Firdaws is its middle and highest; the hadith urges high aspiration in supplication.
أهل الغرف كالكوكب الدري: The people of the chambers are like a brilliant star
تفاوت المنازل في الجنة عظيم، والمنازل ال: The difference between ranks in Paradise is immense, and the high ranks are not reserved for the prophets, but are for those whose faith is true.
جنتان من فضة وجنتان من ذهب: Two gardens of silver and two gardens of gold
هو تفسير لجنتي سورة الرحمن: جنتان من ذهب: It explains the gardens of Surat al-Rahman: two gardens of gold for those brought near, and below them two gardens of silver for the people of the right.
للجنة أبواب ثمانية، ولكل عمل صالح باب يُ: Paradise has eight gates, and each righteous deed has a gate from which its people are called.

نعيم أهل الجنة يتجدد ويزداد، ويزداد حسنه: The bliss of the people of Paradise is ever renewed and increasing, and their beauty grows.
النظر إلى وجه الله أحب نعيم الجنة إلى أه: Looking at the Face of Allah is the dearest bliss of Paradise to its people; with it the Prophet ﷺ explained "the increase" in the verse of Surat Yunus, as in Muslim's next narration.

القرآن شفاء: آيات الشفاء: The Quran is healing: the verses of healing
وصف الله كتابه بأنه شفاء في ستة مواضع، ي: Allah describes His Book as healing in six places, which authors on ruqyah gather under the name "the verses of healing". Healing in them covers the healing of hearts from doubt and desire, and, according to most exegetes, includes healing of bodies through ruqyah and seeking refuge. No authentic text from the Prophet fixes these verses to a number or a manner; they are grouped only because they share the word "healing".
أصرح آية في الباب، وفيها اختلف العلماء:: The clearest verse on the subject. Scholars differed whether it is healing for hearts only or for bodies too through ruqyah, as quoted in the scholars' statements below.
وشفاء لما في الصدور: And healing for what is in the breasts
الموعظة والشفاء والهدى والرحمة أوصاف أرب: Admonition, healing, guidance and mercy are four descriptions of the Quran; healing here is for the diseases of doubts and desires.
الانتفاع بالقرآن شفاءً مشروط بالإيمان به: Benefiting from the Quran as healing depends on believing in it; whoever turns away from it does not benefit.
شفاء الصدور من الغيظ والكرب بنصر الله، و: Healing of the breasts from anger and distress through the victory of Allah; it is among the verses of healing cited by those who practise ruqyah.
يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه فيه شفا: There emerges from their bellies a drink of varying colours, in which there is healing for people
آية العسل، وهي أصل في مشروعية التداوي با: The verse of honey: a basis for using physical remedies alongside ruqyah, and the Prophet ﷺ affirmed it in the hadith of honey.
قول إبراهيم عليه السلام: نسب المرض إلى ن: The words of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: he attributed illness to himself out of courtesy towards Allah and attributed healing to his Lord, for Allah alone is the Healer.
ما يُرقى به من سور القرآن وآياته: The surahs and verses used for ruqyah
القرآن كله يُرقى به، وقد ثبت في السنة تخ: The whole Quran may be recited as ruqyah, and the Sunnah singles out certain surahs and verses for ruqyah and protection: al-Fatihah, the three surahs of refuge, Ayat al-Kursi and the closing verses of al-Baqarah. Scholars also mention verses about the undoing of magic because of their meaning, without an authentic text from the Prophet specifying them.
رقى بها أحد الصحابة سيدَ قوم لُدغ فبرأ،: A Companion recited it as ruqyah over a tribal chief who had been stung, and he recovered; the Prophet ﷺ approved and said: "How did you know it is a ruqyah?" See the hadith in the next chapter.
من قرأها إذا أوى إلى فراشه لم يزل عليه م: Whoever recites it on going to bed remains under a guardian from Allah, as in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in al-Bukhari.
من قرأ بالآيتين من آخر سورة البقرة في لي: Whoever recites the last two verses of al-Baqarah at night, they suffice him; and Satan flees from the house in which al-Baqarah is recited.
كان النبي ﷺ يجمعها مع المعوذتين فينفث في: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite it with the two surahs of refuge, blow lightly into his palms and wipe his body with them every night.
استعاذة من شر الخلق عامة، ومن السحر والح: Seeking refuge from the evil of creation in general, and from magic and envy in particular; the one who casts the evil eye is included in "the envier".
استعاذة بربوبية الله وملكه وألوهيته من ش: Seeking refuge in the Lordship, Sovereignty and Divinity of Allah from the evil of the retreating whisperer, among jinn and mankind.
آيات إبطال السحر في قصة موسى: The verses on undoing magic in the story of Musa
«إن الله سيبطله»: يذكرها أهل العلم في ال: "Allah will surely nullify it": scholars cite these, with the verses of al-A'raf and Ta-Ha from the same story, in ruqyah against magic because of their meaning; no authentic text from the Prophet specifies them.
أحاديث صحيحة في الرقية بالقرآن والأدعية: Authentic hadiths on ruqyah with the Quran and with the Prophet's supplications, each quoted from the books bundled in Mishkat, with its reference number and grade.
التداوي والأخذ بالأسباب: Seeking treatment and taking the means
الرقية لا تعارض الطب؛ فقد أمر النبي ﷺ با: Ruqyah does not oppose medicine. The Prophet ﷺ commanded seeking treatment, told that every disease has a cure, and prescribed honey for one whose stomach was ailing. Combining ruqyah with treatment is the way of the Sunnah.
أقوال العلماء بمصادرها: Statements of scholars with their sources
نقول بلفظها من كتب التفسير المضمّنة في م: Verbatim quotations from the tafsir books bundled in Mishkat, and two quotations from books not bundled, with the location of each.
شروط تجعل الرقية مشروعة، مستخلصة من النص: Conditions that make ruqyah lawful, drawn from the texts and from what scholars have established.
كيف يرقي المسلم نفسه وأهله: How a Muslim performs ruqyah for himself and his family
خطوات عملية مأخوذة من هدي النبي ﷺ، لا تح: Practical steps taken from the guidance of the Prophet ﷺ, needing no intermediary.
ما يجب الحذر منه في باب الرقية، وحديث مش: What must be avoided in ruqyah, and a well-known hadith whose attribution to the Prophet is not authentic.
فيه مشروعية الرقية بالقرآن، وأن الفاتحة: It shows that ruqyah with the Quran is lawful, that al-Fatihah is a ruqyah, and that payment for ruqyah is permitted when it brings benefit.
النفث بالمعوذات عند المرض: Blowing with the surahs of refuge during illness
يرقي المريض نفسه بالمعوذات وينفث، ويجوز: The sick person may recite the surahs of refuge over himself and blow lightly, and another may recite over him and wipe him.
التحصين بالإخلاص والمعوذتين قبل النوم: Protection with al-Ikhlas and the two surahs of refuge before sleep
هيئة الرقية: جمع الكفين، والنفث فيهما، و: The manner of ruqyah: joining the palms, blowing lightly into them, reciting, then wiping as much of the body as one can, three times.
رقية جبريل للنبي ﷺ: The ruqyah of Jibril for the Prophet ﷺ
الرقية بذكر اسم الله والدعاء بالشفاء، وف: Ruqyah by mentioning the name of Allah and supplicating for healing; it shows that the evil eye and envy are among the things ruqyah is made for.
«اللهم رب الناس أذهب الباس»: "O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm"
من أجمع الأدعية النبوية للمريض، يقال مع: One of the most comprehensive prophetic supplications for the sick, said while wiping with the right hand.
وضع اليد على موضع الألم: Placing the hand on the place of pain
يرقي المريض نفسه بيده على موضع الألم: «ب: The sick person recites over himself with his hand on the painful place: "In the name of Allah" three times, then the seeking of refuge seven times.
«لا بأس بالرقى ما لم يكن فيه شرك»: "There is no harm in ruqyah as long as it contains no shirk"
الأصل الجامع في الباب: كل رقية خلت من ال: The comprehensive rule of the subject: every ruqyah free of shirk is permitted, and the Shariah is the reference for judging that.
«من استطاع منكم أن ينفع أخاه فلينفعه»: "Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so"
النهي الأول كان عن رقى الجاهلية، ثم أذن: The earlier prohibition concerned the ruqyahs of the Days of Ignorance; then the Prophet ﷺ permitted what was free of anything forbidden and encouraged Muslims to benefit one another.
الاسترقاء من العين: Seeking ruqyah against the evil eye
العين حق كما في الحديث المتفق عليه، ويشر: The evil eye is real, as in the agreed-upon hadith, and seeking ruqyah against it is prescribed.
الرخصة في الرقية من العين والحمة والنملة: The permission of ruqyah against the evil eye, stings and sores
الحُمة: سم ذوات السموم كالعقرب، والنملة:: Humah is the venom of stinging creatures such as scorpions; namlah are sores that appear on the side. Naming them does not restrict ruqyah to them.
آية الكرسي حفظ من الشيطان: Ayat al-Kursi is protection from Satan
قراءة آية الكرسي عند النوم سبب للحفظ من: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi at bedtime is a means of protection from Satan until morning, and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed it.
خواتيم البقرة تكفي قارئها: The closing verses of al-Baqarah suffice the reciter
قيل: كفتاه من قيام الليل، وقيل: من كل سو: It is said they suffice him in place of night prayer, and it is said they suffice him against every evil; many commentators accept both meanings.
الشيطان ينفر من بيت تقرأ فيه البقرة: Satan flees from a house where al-Baqarah is recited
تحصين البيوت بتلاوة القرآن، وسورة البقرة: Houses are protected by reciting the Quran, and Surat al-Baqarah in particular.
«ما أنزل الله داء إلا أنزل له شفاء»: "Allah has not sent down any disease without sending down a cure for it"
فيه تقوية لنفس المريض ورجاؤه، وحثّ على ط: It strengthens the hope of the sick and urges seeking and researching treatment.
الشفاء بإذن الله عند إصابة الدواء المناس: Healing comes by the permission of Allah when the right remedy is found; this is a basis for diagnosing a disease correctly.
أمر صريح بالتداوي، فطلب العلاج من الأخذ: An explicit command to seek treatment: seeking medical care is part of taking the means that we are commanded to take, and it does not contradict reliance on Allah.
«صدق الله وكذب بطن أخيك»: "Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied"
فيه تصديق قوله تعالى في العسل «فيه شفاء: It confirms the words of Allah about honey, "in it is healing for people", and teaches patience with a remedy until its effect appears.
السبعون ألفاً «لا يسترقون»: The seventy thousand "who do not ask for ruqyah"
لا يطلبون الرقية من غيرهم كمالاً في التو: They do not ask others for ruqyah, out of perfect reliance on Allah. This does not prevent a Muslim from performing ruqyah for himself or others, nor from seeking treatment; the Prophet ﷺ performed ruqyah, received it and commanded treatment.
«إن الرقى والتمائم والتولة شرك»: "Spells, amulets and love charms are shirk"
المراد رقى الجاهلية التي فيها شرك أو كلا: This refers to the ruqyahs of the Days of Ignorance containing shirk or unknown words. Tama'im are objects hung to ward off the evil eye; tiwalah is what is claimed to make a woman beloved to her husband.
«عليكم بالشفاءين: العسل والقرآن»: "Hold fast to the two healings: honey and the Quran"
حديث مشهور على الألسنة، والصواب أنه من ق: A widely quoted hadith. The sound view is that it is the saying of Ibn Mas'ud himself; attributing it to the Prophet ﷺ is weak, as the grades of the hadith scholars shown with it indicate.
قولان في معنى الشفاء، والثاني يدخل فيه ش: Two views on the meaning of healing; the second includes healing of bodies through ruqyah.
شفاء القرآن لأمراض القلوب خاص بمن آمن به: The Quran's healing of the diseases of hearts belongs to whoever believes in it and follows it.
The Quran's healing covers both hearts and bodies.
On Surat al-Falaq: the evil eye stems from envy.
The origin of the three well-known conditions.
فتح الباري، كتاب الطب، باب الرقى بالقرآن: Fath al-Bari, Book of Medicine, chapter on ruqyah with the Quran and the surahs of refuge
الانتفاع بالرقية بقدر صدق الراقي والمرقي: The benefit of ruqyah is in proportion to the sincerity and faith of the reciter and the patient.
زاد المعاد في هدي خير العباد، فصل الطب ا: Zad al-Ma'ad, chapter on prophetic medicine
أن تكون بكلام الله أو بأسمائه وصفاته أو: It must be with the words of Allah, His names and attributes, or transmitted supplications
كالفاتحة والمعوذات وآية الكرسي، و«أذهب ا: Such as al-Fatihah, the surahs of refuge, Ayat al-Kursi, "Remove the harm, Lord of mankind" and "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you"; these are the highest forms of ruqyah and the furthest from doubt.
أن تكون بلسان مفهوم المعنى: It must be in words whose meaning is understood
بالعربية أو بما يُعرف معناه من غيرها، فل: In Arabic or in a language whose meaning is known; ruqyah with talismans, disjointed letters and unknown names is not permitted.
أن يُعتقد أن الشفاء من الله وحده: One must believe that healing is from Allah alone
الرقية سبب لا يؤثر بذاته، والشافي هو الل: Ruqyah is a means that has no effect by itself; Allah is the Healer: "And when I am ill, it is He who heals me".
أن تخلو من الشرك والمحرّم: It must be free of shirk and anything forbidden
قال النبي ﷺ: «لا بأس بالرقى ما لم يكن في: The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no harm in ruqyah as long as it contains no shirk." So no calling on other than Allah, no sacrifice to other than Him, and no seeking help from jinn.
ألا تكون بهيئة محرّمة: It must not be performed in a forbidden manner
كالرقية في الأماكن النجسة، أو مع خلوة با: Such as in impure places, in seclusion with a non-mahram woman or touching what may not be touched, or harming the patient by beating or choking.
ألا تُترك بها الأسباب المشروعة: It must not replace lawful means
الرقية لا تغني عن الطبيب، والنبي ﷺ رقى و: Ruqyah does not replace the physician. The Prophet ﷺ performed ruqyah, sought treatment and commanded it, so a Muslim combines both.
أخلص النية وأحسن الظن بالله: Make your intention sincere and think well of Allah
استحضر أن الشافي هو الله، وأن القرآن شفا: Keep in mind that Allah is the Healer and that the Quran is healing for those who believe in it, and support this with repentance, seeking forgiveness and charity.
ضع يدك على موضع الألم: Place your hand on the place of pain
وقل: «بسم الله» ثلاثاً، ثم «أعوذ بالله و: Say "In the name of Allah" three times, then "I seek refuge in Allah and His power from the evil of what I feel and what I fear" seven times, as in the hadith of 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As.
اقرأ الفاتحة والمعوذات وآية الكرسي: Recite al-Fatihah, the surahs of refuge and Ayat al-Kursi
وما تيسر من آيات الشفاء وخواتيم البقرة،: And whatever is easy of the verses of healing and the end of al-Baqarah, blowing lightly, a gentle breath with a little moisture.
امسح بيدك على جسدك: Wipe your body with your hand
اجمع كفيك وانفث فيهما واقرأ الإخلاص والم: Join your palms, blow lightly into them and recite al-Ikhlas and the two surahs of refuge, then wipe as much of your body as you can, three times.
«اللهم رب الناس، أذهب الباس، اشفه وأنت ا: "O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the harm; heal him, for You are the Healer; there is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no illness behind."
داوم على التحصين واستمر في العلاج: Keep up protection and continue treatment
أذكار الصباح والمساء والنوم حصن يومي، وا: The morning, evening and bedtime remembrances are a daily fortress, and following up with a physician is a duty for anyone who needs it.
من الخطأ الاكتفاء بالرقية في الأمراض الع: It is a mistake to rely on ruqyah alone for physical and mental illnesses and abandon the physician; the Sunnah is to combine both.
تعليق الخيوط والخرز والطلاسم لدفع العين: Hanging threads, beads and talismans to ward off the evil eye or bring benefit is a form of forbidden shirk.
إتيان السحرة والكهنة والعرافين: Going to sorcerers, soothsayers and fortune-tellers
ومن علاماتهم: السؤال عن اسم الأم، وطلب أ: Their signs include asking for the mother's name, requesting an item of the patient's, sacrificing to other than Allah, speaking unintelligible words and claiming knowledge of the unseen.
المبالغة في نسبة كل مرض إلى العين أو الم: Attributing every illness to the evil eye or possession
كثير من الأعراض لها أسباب طبية ونفسية تح: Many symptoms have medical and psychological causes that need diagnosis; hastily attributing them to possession delays treatment and harms the patient.
الإيذاء والاستغلال باسم الرقية: Harm and exploitation in the name of ruqyah
الضرب والخنق والصعق، والمغالاة في الأجور: Beating, choking, electric shocks, excessive fees, and selling water and oils at exorbitant prices on claims of special power are all things the Shariah does not approve.
